title: the siege
hook: a king who leaps into a fight, a messenger who won't be held, and the gates of Lanka
carry: peace offered, even at the gates

segments.voice: Yesterday: the siege began with two spies caught and set free. Rama hid nothing, and they went home telling Ravana to make peace. Did you try having nothing to hide? Today, the last chance for peace, and the gates of Lanka. Day six hundred forty.

Rama climbs Mount Suvela with his leaders to look at Lanka. And there, on a high tower across the way, stands Ravana himself, in royal clothes, with his attendants. Sugriva can't stand it. Without a word to anyone he leaps across, lands on the tower, knocks off Ravana's crown, and the two kings wrestle. Then Sugriva jumps back, pleased with himself. Rama is not pleased. A king doesn't do that, he says. If something had happened to you, what would I have done?
screen: `RAVANA ON HIS TOWER.` → `SUGRIVA LEAPS ACROSS.` → `A KING DOESN'T DO THAT.`

segments.voice: Then Rama does things in order. He sets the army around the city. Lanka has four great gates, and he assigns a leader to each: Nila to the east, Angada to the south, Hanuman to the west, and Rama himself, with Lakshmana, to the north, where Ravana is. Lanka is surrounded. And still, before the first blow, Rama sends a messenger. He chooses Angada, Vali's son. Angada leaps to Ravana's palace and speaks for Rama, plainly: return Sita, and ask pardon, and you'll live. If not, this is the end of your line, and Vibhishana will rule Lanka. Ravana orders him seized. Four rakshasas grab him by the arms. Angada lets them. Then he springs up onto the palace roof with all four still hanging on, and they drop off and fall to the ground. He stamps on the roof's peak and breaks it, and leaps back to Rama. You may have heard a different scene here: Angada planting his foot in Ravana's court, and no one able to lift it. That comes from later tellings, especially Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas. In Valmiki it's the broken rooftop. Either way, the point is the same. Rama gave a final offer of peace, in person, with the city already surrounded. Only after Angada returns does the battle begin. The monkeys swarm the walls with trees and rocks, the rakshasas pour out of the gates, and the siege of Lanka becomes a war.
screen: `FOUR GATES, FOUR LEADERS.` · `ANGADA CARRIES THE LAST OFFER.` · `FOUR RAKSHASAS AND A ROOFTOP.` · `THE FOOT IN COURT CAME LATER.` · then, large: `PEACE OFFERED, EVEN AT THE GATES.`

segments.voice: Sit and let your shoulders drop. Think of a conflict you're in, large or small, at home or at work. You may already feel surrounded, or ready to leap at someone's tower like Sugriva. Pause there. Ask: have I made the last offer of peace, plainly, in person? You don't need to answer now. Just breathe with the question, in and out, until it feels a little less like a war. The bell holds the time.
The siege. Lanka's four gates surrounded, and one last offer of peace carried by Angada, before the first battle begins.
Your line: peace offered, even at the gates. Today, in one disagreement, make a plain offer of peace before anything else. Day six hundred forty.

howItsDone: In North Indian Ramlila performances, Angada's embassy to Ravana's court is a well-known scene, often played in the Ramcharitmanas version with Angada's unmovable foot.

original.note: Sanskrit Aṅgada: Vali's son; the word also names an armlet, an ornament worn on the upper arm.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama attacked as soon as he reached Lanka.
what it means: he surrounded the city, then sent Angada with one more offer of peace.
what a scholar hears: the famous immovable foot of Angada belongs to later tellings, especially Tulsidas; Valmiki has the broken rooftop.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 38–40 (Mount Suvela; Sugriva wrestles Ravana)
